title: Statistical Thinking
description: Interpret and communicate statistics honestly. Tests descriptive stats, hypothesis testing, and the ability to spot misleading analysis.

seo.overviewTitle: Statistical Analysis & A/B Testing Hypothesis Testing
seo.overviewBody: Data-driven decisions require rigorous statistical validation. Employers look for candidates who design A/B test experiments, conduct hypothesis tests (t-test, chi-square, ANOVA), interpret p-values correctly, and calculate confidence intervals.

deliverables.title: 1. A/B Test Experimentation Specification
deliverables.desc: Experiment plan specifying null/alternative hypotheses, sample size calculations, and primary metrics.

deliverables.title: 2. Python Statistical Analysis Script
deliverables.desc: Python script using scipy.stats to run two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and confidence interval calculations.

deliverables.title: 3. Statistical Findings & Decision Report
deliverables.desc: Report evaluating statistical significance (p-value), effect size, and practical business recommendations.

faqs.question: What does a p-value less than 0.05 actually mean?
faqs.answer: A p-value < 0.05 indicates there is less than a 5% probability that the observed result occurred by random chance under the null hypothesis.

faqs.question: What is A/B test peeking bias?
faqs.answer: Peeking bias occurs when analysts check experiment results continuously and stop the test early as soon as p < 0.05, artificially inflating false positive rates.

faqs.question: How do you calculate required sample sizes for an A/B test?
faqs.answer: Sample sizes are calculated using statistical power (typically 80%), significance level (alpha = 0.05), baseline conversion rate, and Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE).
